title: rk convention profile v1
description: The versioned, committed normalisation contract a campaign checks its own notation and statements AGAINST. Lives at `.rk/conventions/<name>.v<n>.json` and is named in `.rk/config.json` as `conventionProfile: "<name>.v<n>"` (the reference key is the filename stem, no `.json`). Deliberately kept OUTSIDE the artifact being checked (LB5, docs/reviews/2026-08-20-qpcp-plan-tierA-codex.md): a register that declares its own tracked classes can shrink its own coverage silently. Gate 9 (notation) enforces `tracked_classes`; the config gate validates this file's shape and its coverage-shrink rule. Schema changes here are compat events (CLAUDE.md rule 10).

schema_version.description: Exactly the string "1". A future incompatible profile shape must never silently run under v1 semantics.

name.description: The profile family name. MUST equal the `<name>` part of the containing filename `<name>.v<n>.json` — a profile whose declared name disagrees with its own path cannot be referenced unambiguously.

version.description: The COMPAT COUNTER (CLAUDE.md rule 10's "bumps a version field"), not a restatement of the filename. Removing a `tracked_classes` entry present in `<name>.v<n-1>.json` is permitted ONLY when this number is strictly greater than that file's own `version` — the config gate's `class-removed-without-bump` check. Copying a profile to a new filename, deleting a class, and leaving `version` untouched is exactly the silent coverage shrink that rule exists to forbid.

tracked_classes.description: The symbol classes Gate 9 enforces. EXPLICIT symbol lists, never patterns: a pattern silently widens or narrows what is tracked as the register grows, and a reader cannot tell which symbols a class covers by reading it.

class.description: Class id, unique within the profile. A notation shard's `class:` frontmatter field must name one of these.

description.description: What the class is, in one line. Read by humans only; never a validity input.

symbols.description: The raw tokens considered tracked for this class, verbatim as the literature writes them — e.g. ["\\epsilon", "\\varepsilon", "\\lambda_{\\min}", "c", "QMA"]. Whitespace is forbidden (a token is one lexical unit); everything else is admitted, because a source's notation is not rk's to constrain. Gate 9's LEXICAL enforcement covers exactly the subset that is a plain LaTeX macro token `\name`: those must be a registered `symbol:` of a notation shard in this class wherever Gate 9 scans, or it is an `unregistered-symbol` ERROR. Tokens outside that shape (bare identifiers, brace/subscript forms) cannot be scanned for reliably and are counted, per class, in Gate 9's coverage line as NOT lexically enforceable — visible, never silently dropped.

blessed.description: The campaign's single blessed macro for this class, e.g. "\\gapfrac" — the one form shards and records are meant to write. Always a plain macro token, so it is always lexically enforceable, and it is tracked whether or not it also appears in `symbols`.

symbols_must_be_registered.description: OPTIONAL, and always true when present. v1 admits no advisory class — the rule holds for every tracked class whether or not this field is written — so any value other than true is a malformed profile, never a quiet opt-out of Gate 9. Kept as an explicit, readable declaration and as the extension point if a later schema version ever admits an advisory class.

lattices.description: Named value orders. Each is an object tagged by `kind`, never a bare array — an untagged list cannot say whether its middle is honestly comparable. `chain` is a total order, written WEAKEST FIRST. `poset` is a partial order given by explicit covering `edges`, for a key whose middle is genuinely incomparable (e.g. reduction classes: quasi-poly and quantum-poly are not ordered, and linearising them silently over-accepts). There is no polarity field: direction is expressed on the signature side, where a parameter is an INTERVAL over these values rather than a point (rk-8805). Gate 9 does not read lattices; the signature entailment check (Check 17) does.

values.description: Ordered WEAKEST FIRST (e.g. ["inv-poly", "inv-log", "const"]). The order is the contract: a consumer compares positions, never strings.
The carrier set. Unordered here — `edges` carries the order.

edges.description: Covering relations as `[weaker, stronger]` pairs. Both endpoints must be declared in `values`, and the relation must be a DAG — a cycle would make two distinct values mutually entailing, which is not an order at all.

choices.description: Normalisation choices the campaign has fixed: which convention is CANONICAL, and which other conventions may appear as declared translations of it. A convention outside `allowed_translations` is not a translation, it is a different statement.

notes.description: OPTIONAL prose: the conversion formulas, the checked source divergences, what a record must state. Read by humans and by model lanes; never a validity input — a gate never parses this.

enums.description: Closed value sets the campaign's records and signatures draw from (hardness classes, reduction classes, ...). Empty object is legitimate on day one.
